answer: The umber detector writes to knoll, and ember shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 213 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 101 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 36 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
